other_failure_modes.name: Target leakage in target encoding
other_failure_modes.description: Target encoding is computed on the training set and mapped directly back to the same training instances without using out-of-fold calculations. This allows the model to memorize the target, leading to severe overfitting.

other_failure_modes.name: Train/test feature mismatch due to stateful logic
other_failure_modes.description: The logic for selecting top features for interactions uses correlation with the target during training, but blindly selects the first N columns during validation/inference. This results in different features being engineered for train vs test, which are then zeroed out during column alignment.

other_failure_modes.name: Inconsistent transformation based on batch statistics
other_failure_modes.description: Applying transformations like one-hot encoding conditionally based on the number of unique values in the current batch/split. If a validation or test set has a different number of unique values than the training set, the transformation might be skipped entirely, causing a mismatch in features.

summary: The solution implements a reasonable ensemble of gradient boosted trees but contains critical bugs in its feature engineering pipeline. Target encoding is applied without out-of-fold techniques, causing massive target leakage. Furthermore, the feature engineering logic for interactions, ratios, and one-hot encoding changes behavior based on the specific split being processed, resulting in mismatched features between train and test sets that are ultimately zeroed out.
